new.title: Admire the Kaiserdom and the Bamberger Reiter
new.desc: Bamberg Cathedral was consecrated in 1012 under Henry II and rebuilt in the 13th century in late Romanesque and early Gothic style. It holds the tomb of Henry II and Kunigunde, Pope Clement II's grave and the Bamberger Reiter equestrian statue.
new.tip: Free to enter; avoid Mass times. Climb Domberg early for fewer crowds.

new.title: Photograph the Altes Rathaus on its river island
new.desc: The Old Town Hall stands on an artificial island in the Regnitz, between the bishop's hill town and the citizens' island town. The Baroque and Rococo facade dates from 1744 to 1756 and has frescoes with protruding figures.
new.tip: Best views from the Obere Brücke; it houses the Ludwig porcelain collection.

new.title: Tour the Neue Residenz and its State Gallery
new.desc: The New Residence was built from 1602 as seat of the prince-bishops and houses the state rooms, including the Imperial Hall, and a branch of the Bavarian State Painting Collections. It served the bishops until 1802.
new.tip: State rooms are visited on guided tours; combine with the Rosengarten terrace.

new.title: Smell the Bamberg Rosengarten above the roofs
new.desc: The rose garden in the inner courtyard of the Neue Residenz has roughly 4,500 roses in many varieties. It offers a view over the old town to Michaelsberg.
new.tip: Free and open daily in season; best in June when the roses bloom.

new.title: Visit Kloster Michaelsberg and its Himmelsgarten ceiling
new.desc: The former Benedictine abbey on Michaelsberg was founded in 1015 and later rebuilt in Baroque style. Its church has a ceiling painted with a garden of plants, the Himmelsgarten, and a terrace with a view of the town.
new.tip: Church has an entry fee for the ceiling; terrace views are free.

new.title: Climb up to the Altenburg castle
new.desc: Altenburg crowns the highest of Bamberg's seven hills and was a bishops' residence from the 14th century. The tower offers views across the city and the Bamberg basin.
new.tip: Reached on foot from Laurenziplatz in about 25 minutes; check current opening of the tower.

new.title: Stroll along Klein-Venedig's fishermen houses
new.desc: The riverside row of half-timbered former fishermen's houses along the Regnitz is nicknamed Little Venice. Many houses have wooden balconies over the water.
new.tip: Best light in the afternoon; boat tours pass here.

new.title: Cross the Untere Brücke for the classic river view
new.desc: The Untere Brücke links the Bergstadt and Inselstadt near the Altes Rathaus. From it you see the river and the Klein-Venedig row.
new.tip: Quiet at sunrise; combine with a walk along Am Leinritt.

new.title: Step into the Gothic Obere Pfarre
new.desc: The Church of Our Lady, begun in 1392, is the only purely Gothic church in the city. It contains the Maria Immaculata altar of Veit Stoß.
new.tip: Free to enter; the tower gives views over the Bergstadt.

new.title: See the Kaisergewänder at the Diözesanmuseum
new.desc: The museum in the Kapitelhaus designed by Balthasar Neumann in 1731 to 1733 shows treasures of the cathedral and diocese. Highlights include the imperial vestments and the Domkreuz.
new.tip: Combined tickets with other Domberg museums are available.

new.title: Explore the city's past at the Historisches Museum
new.desc: The Historical Museum occupies the Alte Hofhaltung, the former bishop's residence next to the cathedral. Its collections cover the history of Bamberg from the Middle Ages onward.
new.tip: Combine with the Alte Hofhaltung courtyard.

new.title: Walk through the historic Vogelsaal at the Naturkundemuseum
new.desc: The Natural History Museum is housed in the former Jesuit college and covers geology, minerals and local fauna. Its historic bird hall is more than 200 years old.
new.tip: Good for rainy days and families.

new.title: Discover the Gärtner- und Häckermuseum
new.desc: The museum tells of the market gardeners and wine growers of Bamberg's Gärtnerstadt, in a preserved gardener's house in Mittelstraße. A 2026 exhibition covers electrification in a gardener's household.
new.tip: Seasonal opening with a winter break; check dates before visiting.

new.title: Visit the Karmelitenkloster on the Kaulberg
new.desc: The Carmelite monastery on the Kaulberg goes back to a 12th-century foundation and was redesigned in Baroque style at the end of the 17th century.
new.tip: Dates of origin vary by source; quiet cloister.

new.title: Drink Aecht Schlenkerla Rauchbier at the historic tavern
new.desc: The Schlenkerla tavern in the former Haus zum blauen Löwen on Dominikanerstraße serves the world-famous Aecht Schlenkerla Rauchbier, brewed at Stephansberg. The beer is drawn from wooden barrels.
new.tip: Order a Schäuferla or Bamberger Zwiebel with it; busy evenings.

new.title: Enjoy the view from the Spezial-Keller beer garden
new.desc: Spezial brews Rauchbier and runs a Keller with a beer garden above the original lager cellars on Stephansberg and a wood-paneled taproom. Many visitors rate its view over the old town as the best in the city.
new.tip: Open in warm season; go at sunset.

new.title: Try a Ungespundet at Mahrs Bräu
new.desc: Mahr's Bräu in Wunderburg is a Bamberg institution since 1602, praised for brewing many styles consistently well. The unfiltered Ungespundet-Hefetrüb is the house signature.
new.tip: Hearty Franconian food; open evenings.

new.title: Taste the Bambergator Doppelbock at Fässla
new.desc: Brauerei Fässla brews since 1649 and is known for its strong Bambergator Doppelbock. Its tavern stands on Obere Königstraße.
new.tip: Try the Bambergator with a hearty Brotzeit.

new.title: Sip Herren Pils at Brauerei Keesmann
new.desc: Keesmann in Wunderburg is known for its Herren Pils, called one of the best in town. The tavern serves traditional Franconian dishes.
new.tip: Garden seating in summer.

new.title: Sit in the Greifenklau beer garden below the Altenburg
new.desc: Greifenklau claims to be one of the oldest Bamberg beer cellars and has a beer garden with about 500 seats behind the tavern. The cellar lies below Altenburg and is part of the UNESCO site.
new.tip: Come after a hike to Altenburg; Keller season only.

new.title: Eat Schäuferla at Zum Sternla
new.desc: Zum Sternla is described as Bamberg's oldest inn and has been a brewpub since 2019. The signature dish is Schäuferla, shoulder roast in beer sauce with a Franconian dumpling.
new.tip: Opening days vary by listing; reserve evenings.

new.title: Bring your own Brotzeit to the Wilde Rose Keller
new.desc: Wilde Rose Keller on Stephansberg has roughly 1,500 seats and lets guests bring their own food, unlike most cellars. It was formerly called Leichtskeller.
new.tip: Seasonal; the 2026 season opened on 30 April.
new.q: Wilde Rose Keller, Oberer Stephansberg 49, Bamberg

new.title: Drink house-brewed beer at the Ambräusianum
new.desc: Ambräusianum is a brewpub in the old town and one of the traditional Bamberg brewery taverns. It brews its own beers on site.
new.tip: Try the seasonal specials.

new.title: Taste dark Klosterbräu beer by the Regnitz
new.desc: Klosterbräu is one of the old Bamberg breweries with a tavern near the Obere Mühlbrücke. It is known for its dark Braunbier.
new.tip: Riverside seating in summer.

new.title: Eat Franconian Schäuferla at Zum Kachelofen
new.desc: Kachelofen is a Gasthaus in the old town with over 40 years of history, known for hearty meat dishes. Reviews highlight its Schäuferla with Wirsing.
new.tip: Often full; reserve.

new.title: Try Franconian classics at Alt-Ringlein
new.desc: Alt-Ringlein on Dominikanerstraße serves Schäuferla, Haxen, Bratwürste and Sauerbraten in a traditional hotel restaurant.
new.tip: Near Schlenkerla; good for a larger meal.

new.title: Learn brewing at the Fränkisches Brauereimuseum
new.desc: The museum in the historic vaults of the Benedictine brewery on Michaelsberg shows Franconian brewing tradition.
new.tip: Small entry fee; combine with Michaelsberg.

new.title: Glide through Bamberg on a gondola
new.desc: Two Franconian gondoliers offer rides on the Regnitz through the old town with individual routes, passing Klein-Venedig.
new.tip: Book ahead; check the season.

new.title: Take a river boat tour from the Kranen
new.desc: Boat excursions start in the heart of the old town and pass Klein-Venedig and several bridges toward the harbour.
new.tip: Check the seasonal timetable.

new.title: Paddle the Regnitz past Little Venice
new.desc: Guided canoe tours in 10-seat canoes pass the Regnitz meadows, Theresian park and Klein-Venedig. A new canoe staircase opened at Wegmannufer in 2026.
new.tip: Warm season; book in advance.

new.title: Walk through the Hain park
new.desc: The Stadtpark Hain, with Theresienhain and Luisenhain, is a historic garden monument and protected landscape. The main entrance is at Mühlwörth and paths lead toward Bug.
new.tip: Free all day.

new.title: Follow the Flusspfad along the Regnitz
new.desc: The river trail has 23 information panels on the history of the Regnitz and the city, with audio guides in German and English.
new.tip: Start near Schloss Geyerswörth; allow about 90 minutes.

new.title: Stroll the Stephansberg beer-cellar trail
new.desc: The Stephansberg hill holds several Bamberg beer cellars with garden terraces, the classic Keller area. The season runs from spring to autumn.
new.tip: Sunny afternoons; bring cash.

new.title: Catch the Bamberger Symphoniker at the Konzerthalle
new.desc: The Bamberger Symphoniker play their home concerts in the Konzert- und Kongresshalle on Mußstraße. The orchestra has carried the title Bayerische Staatsphilharmonie since 2003.
new.tip: Check the season program online.

new.title: Join a Welterbe tour from the Tourist-Information
new.desc: The Tourist Information and Welterbe Visitor Centre near Schloss Geyerswörth offers guided walks on the UNESCO old town and the Regnitz.
new.tip: Book online or at the desk.
